_readme: Hand-authored weekly grid for the ABC station in /otr Station mode (station.js). Edit freely; station.js reads it at load.
Times are the LISTENER'S LOCAL time of day, the way an affiliate carried the network feed: 7:30 is 7:30 wherever you are.
The grid is a composite: each slot is a real day-and-time pairing from one ABC (or NBC Blue, ABC's predecessor) season,
but neighbouring slots may come from different seasons. 'src' says which season and where it was checked.
conf: verified = printed in a season ratings table (Jim Ramsburg, GOld Time Radio); likely = standard reference
knowledge, not re-checked today; approx = the day is confirmed by the catalog's episode dates, the hour is placed by
judgment; fill = not an ABC program, a labelled stand-in for an hour ABC filled with something nobody recorded.
days: 0=Sunday .. 6=Saturday. at: HH:MM local. len: minutes. show: a catalog id or a station-only id from abc.shows.json.
pool: instead of show, pick from a named pool (seeded, so every listener in a time zone hears the same thing).
Hours no slot covers fall to 'defaults' by hour. Overlapping slots are an error (python3 scripts/otr_station_harvest.py --check).
Chain rule (James, Oct 2026): episodes play back to back with no commercials; whenever one ends, the next comes from whichever
show owns the slot at that minute, so a half hour sometimes gets two episodes and the lineup runs a few minutes late.
minLeft: a show never starts with fewer than this many minutes left in its slot; the next slot's owner starts early instead
(keeps a 58-minute Stop the Music from triggering a second hour). 0 = the strict rule.
name: ABC
tagline: What ABC was carrying at this hour, this day of the week, 1945-53
blurb: A composite week of the American Broadcasting Company (the NBC Blue Network until 1945): The Lone Ranger on Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 7:30, The Fat Man and This Is Your FBI on Friday nights, Bing Crosby's Philco Radio Time on Wednesday at 10, Stop the Music and Walter Winchell on Sunday, the 5 o'clock serials for the kids. Episodes run back to back with no commercials, so a half hour slot often fits two. Your local clock, like an affiliate.

slots.label: Breakfast Club hour
slots.src: Don McNeill's Breakfast Club held ABC 9-10 AM for 35 years; archive.org has no usable recordings, so morning fill plays here
Breakfast in Hollywood, Blue/ABC weekdays 11:00 AM, 1943-48 (Tom Breneman)
Ethel and Albert, ABC weekday quarter hour 1944-50; the exact slot moved around the afternoon
Ladies Be Seated, Blue/ABC weekdays 3:00 PM, 1944-50 (Johnny Olson)
Paul Whiteman Club, ABC weekdays 3:30-4:30 PM, 1946-47; plays his ABC hours and 1943 Blue summer shows
Hop Harrigan, Blue/ABC weekdays 4:45 PM, 1942-46
Terry and the Pirates, Blue/ABC weekdays 5:00 PM, 1943-48 (Quaker)
Dick Tracy, Blue/ABC weekdays 5:15 PM, 1943-48 (Tootsie Rolls)
Jack Armstrong, ABC Mon/Wed/Fri 5:30 PM, 1947-50 (Wheaties); two quarter-hour chapters fill the half hour
Tom Corbett, Space Cadet, ABC Tue/Thu 5:30 PM, Jan-Jul 1952 (episode dates confirm Tue/Thu); Sky King held the slot 1947-50

slots.label: Local news and sports
slots.src: Affiliates ran local news here; Bill Stern's sports reel and wartime Winchell and Pearson commentaries stand in
Easy Aces, NBC Blue Tue/Wed/Thu 7:00 PM, 1935-42 (Anacin)

slots.label: Headline Edition
slots.src: ABC's 7:00 news strip; no recordings, sports and commentary fill

slots.label: Elmer Davis and the News
slots.src: Elmer Davis held ABC 7:15 PM 1945-53; no recordings on archive.org, so commentary and sports fill
The Lone Ranger, ABC Mon/Wed/Fri 7:30 PM, 1942-54 (1947-48 ratings table: MWF 7:30 30 ABC)
The Green Hornet, ABC Tuesday and Thursday nights 1947-48 (General Mills); episode dates confirm Tue/Thu
Counter-Spy, ABC Tue/Thu 7:30 PM, 1948-49, alternating nights with The Lone Ranger (1948-49 season page)
The Railroad Hour, ABC Monday 8:00 PM, Oct 1948-Jun 1949 (45 minutes until April, then 30; NBC from the fall). The 45-minute shows run over, as the chain rule allows
Lum and Abner, Blue/ABC 8:15 PM Mon-Thu, 1941-47 (Alka-Seltzer); the half hour holds two chapters
The Fat Man, ABC Friday 8:00 PM, 1946-51 (1947-51 ratings tables: Fri 8:00 30 ABC); Richard Diamond took the slot in 1951-52
Sherlock Holmes, ABC Monday 8:30 PM, 1946-47 (Kreml)
Duffy's Tavern, Blue Network Tuesday 8:30 PM, 1942-44 (1943-44 ratings table: Tue 8:30 30 Blue)
